subject: Hosted API intermittent latency — visibility brief & remediation plan
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@starnet.ai>; SRE Team <sre@starnet.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API intermittent latency — visibility brief & remediation plan

Hi Olivia / Starnet SRE team,

Quick update — starting ~07:50 PST we observed intermittent p95 latency elevations (hosted text-generation endpoint) affecting some customer traffic routed through our us-west pool. The impact has been visible on your integration as increased 95th percentile latency and occasional token-stream stalls; your telemetry spike roughly aligns with what we saw.

What we know so far:
- Window: ~07:50–09:10 PST (ongoing at initial detection)
- Symptom: p95 latency up to ~2.6s (baseline ~1.1s) for short sequences; brief streaming stalls reported by some clients
- Scope: routed to us-west serving pool; a subset of shared-hosted capacity only — no data plane errors (503/500) observed for your account

Immediate mitigations in progress:
- Scaling: we’ve proactively increased serving capacity in the affected pool to absorb burst load (temporary).
- Routing: enabling conservative fallback routing to other healthy pools where model variants are compatible.
- Observation: kernel telemetry collection and request traces are live; we are collecting KV-cache and batching metrics.

Attachments: we’re attaching a short pulse log (incident-pulse-log.csv) for your reference and an internal remediation runbook we will use during postmortem.

We’ll keep this thread for direct comms. Ben (cc) is leading the technical investigation and will post updates; I’ll follow up with an ETA and next steps once we confirm stabilization.

Apologies for the disruption — we know low-latency is critical for your workflow.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwoodinference.com

> Quick update — starting ~07:50 PST we observed intermittent p95 latency elevations (hosted text-generation endpoint) affecting some customer traffic routed through our us-west pool.

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@starnet.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API intermittent latency — visibility brief & remediation plan

Hi team — investigation notes / current status: 

Observation summary:
- Root driver appears to be a combination of transient kernel scheduling delays on a subset of GPU nodes + elevated prefix-cache churn for the specific model family your integration uses. Churn increased KV lookups which amplified tail latency under burst traffic.
- No request-level errors; suggestion: higher latency only, so client-side retries will increase load and may worsen the tail.

Actions taken (completed):
- Scaled additional capacity in us-west and warmed standby nodes (08:25 PST).
- Enabled cross-pool routing for compatible model variants (08:40 PST) which reduced observed p95 by ~30% in telemetry.
- Throttling rule: temporarily tightened token-queue admission for best-effort tiers to protect SLOs of reserved customers (08:50 PST).

Ongoing actions:
- We are flushing stale KV entries on three affected nodes and stabilizing cache TTLs (in progress).
- Kernel-level patch queued and will be applied in a controlled roll starting 12:15 PST; we’ve validated the patch on a small canary.

Recommended customer guidance:
- Please avoid aggressive retry backoffs for the 09:00 batch; if possible, delay the non-critical batch by 20–30 minutes while we finish cache stabilization.
- If you must run at 09:00, set conservative retry jitter (initial backoff 500ms, max retries 2).

References and artifacts:
- Pulse log attached (incident-pulse-log.csv) — contains a short slice of p95 metrics and request trace ids.
- Tracking Jira: RED-4321 (https://jira.redwoodinference.com/browse/RED-4321)

I’ll post another update once the cache flush completes and after patch rollout begins.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
ben@redwoodinference.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-12-05T14:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API intermittent latency — visibility brief & remediation plan

Hi Olivia — sending a final operational update for the incident window.

Summary (final):
- Stabilized by 14:10 PST after cache flushes completed and kernel patch rollout to the affected nodes.
- Observed p95 returned to baseline (~1.1s) on our post-rollout telemetry. No further streaming stalls reported in the sampled traces.
- Impact: transient p95 elevation for ~07:50–14:10 PST; we estimate ~2.1% of requests from your traffic saw >1.8s tail latency during the window.

Next steps and follow-up:
- We’ve opened a formal incident postmortem (RED-4321) and will share a 1-page RCA within 48 hours.
- Proposed working session: Wed 2026-12-08 10:00 PST to walk through RCA, mitigation improvements, and any changes you’d like to prioritize in runbook. Please let me know if that time works.
- In the meantime, we attached the remediation runbook excerpt used during the event (remediation-runbook.pdf).

Apologies again for the disruption. We’ll include a concrete set of service-level mitigations (routing rules, cache heuristics, and improved kernel rollout gating) in the postmortem.

If you want to escalate to a bridge now, we’re available — otherwise I’ll schedule the follow-up and share the invite.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwoodinference.com
